← Return to Kanji Path

Shared knowledge. Free tools.

Kanji Path is an independent study app. Its interface and source are provided under the MIT licence. Upstream educational data retains its original licences.

  • Kanji meanings, readings, school grades, stroke counts and frequency derive from KANJIDIC / KANJIDIC2, copyright Jim Breen and the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group. Project · CC BY-SA 4.0 and licence conditions. The bundled data is an adapted subset of 2,136 Jōyō kanji, serialized to compact JSON.
  • The JSON conversion is from David Luz Gouveia’s kanji-data (MIT). WaniKani-specific material is excluded. JLPT estimates originate with Jonathan Waller’s resources and are unofficial study aids, not official exam lists.
  • Stroke paths are from KanjiVG, copyright Ulrich Apel and contributors, under CC BY-SA 3.0. Modifications: select 2,136 kanji and 92 kana, extract ordered SVG paths, serialize as compact JSON. Adapted stroke data remains CC BY-SA 3.0.
  • Basic kana, 127 vocabulary entries and 40 original beginner practice sentences are provided under CC0. These examples are introductory material rather than a complete grammar curriculum.
  • Scheduling uses an SM-2-style calculation implemented locally. Shape matching compares user strokes geometrically against KanjiVG. Audio uses the device’s Japanese speech synthesis voice.

Snapshot date: 21 October 2026. See the source repository’s scripts/build-data.py and README for the refresh procedure. App data and participant progress are stored in the browser. Export backups regularly.
